selected_script.angle: Mopping over dark kitchen grout only wets the tile and leaves the grimy grout lines behind
selected_script.hook: I kept mopping this spot, but the grout line just stayed dark and streaky.

timeline.0-3s: Extreme close-up of a dirty ceramic kitchen tile grout line with gray-brown embedded grime; a regular wet mop passes over it and the tile gets shiny while the grout line stays dark.
timeline.3-6s: The same mop scrubs back and forth harder on the same grout line, spreading cloudy dirty water into the tile edges and leaving residue, with a slight frustrated hand movement.
timeline.6-10s: The Grout Cleaner Kit enters from beside the cabinet: the white 32 oz Grout-eez bottle with red and blue label and ribbed white neck is shown briefly, cleaner is applied to the same grout line, then the bright blue V-shaped brush head with dense white twisted nylon bristles attached to a plain standard threaded pole scrubs along the grout; the camera holds a comparable close-up showing the cleaned section visibly lighter beside the still-dirty section, ending with a natural voiceover light CTA.

script_record.voiceover: I kept mopping it, but the grout still looked dirty. Then I used Grout-eez with the V-brush on the same line. Way easier to see what’s actually clean—try it on ceramic or porcelain tile.
